finding: CF-A-CARD-LINE-IS-NOT-A-RUNG-IN-A-HEADING-EITHER (#2023, Drew 2026-09-09). baseballcardpedia nests card rosters inside the Parallels section as <h3>/<h4> SUBSECTIONS, and the ladder reader's heading loop -- unlike its <li> loop, which has refused card lines since D33 -- never asked whether a heading was a card line. BCP builds a heading id by replacing spaces with underscores, so "BDP175_Colby_Rasmus_AU_RC" detagged to "BDP175 Colby Rasmus AU RC" and became a PARALLEL of every base card on the page. These 1729 rows on 2005 upper-deck-first-pitch carry 10 distinct such parallels: the row's "parallel" names ANOTHER CARD, often another player entirely (a Verlander BDP129 row whose parallel is "BDP175 Colby Rasmus AU RC"). A row whose parallel is another card is not a card and has no address, so it is RETIRED rather than repointed -- there is no correct destination to guess, and guessing one is what "one card, one row, one pool" forbids. Sales: measured read-only 2026-09-09, the whole 57,803-row population carries ONE sale, so keepSales:true leaves it for the GREAT REMATCH to re-place from the sale title rather than onto a guessed address. Every row is from the LEGACY baseballcardpedia / baseballcardpedia-graded scrapes; the census confirmed ZERO rows from any baseballcardpedia-ladders-* source, and the reader fix in this PR closes the hole so the next scrape cannot recreate them.
